citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice and the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On the periodic box $T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, take smooth real periodic charge and current densities $ho,\mathbf J$, smooth periodic $\mathbf A,\dot{\mathbf A},\phi$, and $L,\epsilon_0,\mu_0>0$. Define the formal classical density
$$\mathcal L= rac{\epsilon_0}{2}|\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi|^2- rac1{2\mu_0}|
abla	imes\mathbf A|^2-ho\phi+\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf A.$$
The canonical momenta are $ oldsymbol\pi_A=\epsilon_0(\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi)$ and $\pi_\phi=0$. Periodic integration by parts gives
$$H=\int_{T_L^3}\left( rac{| oldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\epsilon_0}+ rac{|
abla	imes\mathbf A|^2}{2\mu_0} +\phi(
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho)-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf Aight)d^3x.$$
Variation of the multiplier $\phi$ imposes $
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho=0$. In Coulomb gauge $
abla\cdot\mathbf A=0$, this becomes $-\Delta\phi=ho/\epsilon_0$. Such a smooth periodic solution exists only if $\int_{T_L^3}ho\,d^3x=0$. If this neutrality condition holds, there is a unique zero-mean solution, with Fourier coefficients
$$\widehat\phi_0=0,\qquad \widehat\phi_k= rac{\widehatho_k}{\epsilon_0|2\pi k/L|^2}\quad(k
e0),\qquad \widehatho_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}ho(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,d^3x.$$
It is smooth and satisfies
$$ rac{\epsilon_0}{2}\int|
abla\phi|^2\,d^3x = rac12\intho\phi\,d^3x = rac{L^3}{2\epsilon_0}\sum_{k
e0} rac{|\widehatho_k|^2}{|2\pi k/L|^2}\ge0.$$
This is a classical conditional solver for smooth periodic neutral data; it makes no claim about quantum density products or nonperiodic boundary conditions.

derivations.claim:
Integrating [F1] over $[0,L]^3$ gives
$$\int_{[0,L]^3}-\Delta\phi\,d^3x =-\sum_{j=1}^3\int_0^{L}\!\int_{[0,L]^2}\partial_j^2\phi\,d^2x_{\widehat j}\,dx_j=0,$$
because for each $j$ the integral in $x_j$ is the difference of the periodic values of $\partial_j\phi$ at $L$ and $0$.

The right side of the same integrated equation is
$$\epsilon_0^{-1}\int_{[0,L]^3}\rho_0\,d^3x=\epsilon_0^{-1}\rho_0L^3\ne0,$$
contradicting step 1.1. Thus no smooth periodic solution exists for this nonzero total charge; the same integration proves neutrality is necessary for any periodic solution.
